- When sentiment is negative and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model should not overcorrect upward; cap forecast rise to 2–3% above prior high.  
- If forecast overshoots true outcome by >5% in early days of 30d horizon, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model should underweight short-term volatility and favor smoother, lower trendlines.  
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after a dip, model should not underestimate the rebound — adjust forecast to align with sentiment’s “recovery bias” (e.g., +1.5–2.5% per day if sentiment > 0.1).  
- Avoid forecasting “sudden drops” unless sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) — if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, forecast should not dip below 1–2% below prior low.
